title: Presentable approximations of a fixed cellular tree with compatible supports
statement:
Use the universe, regularity, presentability, weak saturation and $L$-tree definitions in [lem-coef-weak-saturation-tree-presentation]. Let $\tau$ be uncountable regular and let $\mathcal A$ be an ordinary locally $\tau$-presentable category with small Hom sets: it has all small colimits and is generated under small $\tau$-filtered colimits by a small family of $\tau$-presentable objects. Let $L$ be an arrow class in $\mathcal A$. Fix a $\tau$-good $L$-tree with root $X$, small indexing poset $T$, and specified attaching arrows $P_t\to Q_t$ in $L$. No weak-equivalence class is part of these data.

There exist a small $\tau$-filtered poset $P$, an inclusion-increasing family of downward-closed subsets $S_p\subseteq T$ with $|S_p|<\tau$, and a diagram $p\mapsto h_p:M_p\to N_p$ in the arrow category, with $\tau$-presentable endpoints, satisfying the following properties. Each $h_p$ is the colimit arrow of an $L$-tree on $S_p$ with root $M_p$ and the specified attaching arrows indexed by $S_p$. There are compatible root maps $M_p\to X$ and isomorphisms from the objectwise pushouts of these trees along $M_p\to X$ to the original restricted trees on $S_p$. For $p\leq p'$, the transition square of arrows extends to maps between the trees on the common cells, respecting root maps, predecessor colimit maps and both legs of every specified attaching square, with the identity on $P_t$ and $Q_t$; these maps compose and the pushout identifications are compatible with them. The resulting cocone $h_p\to(X\to Y_T)$ is colimiting in the arrow category. For every $E\subseteq T$ with $|E|<\tau$, there is $p\in P$ with $E\subseteq S_p$.

For every nonempty filtered subposet $Q\subseteq P$ in its inherited order, put $S_Q=\bigcup_{q\in Q}S_q$, $M_Q=\operatorname{colim}_{q\in Q}M_q$, $N_Q=\operatorname{colim}_{q\in Q}N_q$, and let $h_Q:M_Q\to N_Q$ be the arrow colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The arrow $h_Q$ is the colimit arrow of an $L$-tree on $S_Q$ with root $M_Q$ and the specified attaching arrows indexed by $S_Q$. The canonical square with top arrow $h_Q$, bottom arrow $X\to Y_{S_Q}$ and left leg $M_Q\to X$ is a pushout. In particular $h_Q$ lies in the weakly saturated closure of $L$.

source.place: Lemma A.2.6.9, proof observation (ii), printed p. 822; the compatible compact-root descent input expands the compactness construction in Lemma A.1.5.11, printed pp. 806-807. Agent-formulated auxiliary statement, not a separately numbered assertion of HTT. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag for this cellular-tree assertion.

proof.text: Fix a small $\tau$-filtered presentation of $X$ by $\tau$-presentable objects. By [lem-coef-cardinal-filtered-poset-reindex], reindex it as $X=\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}X_i$, with $I$ a small $\tau$-filtered poset. For every $i$, the tail $I_{\ge i}$ is $\tau$-filtered and still presents $X$. Indeed upper bounds are obtained by adjoining $i$ to the prescribed set of indices. A cocone on the tail extends to $I$ by sending $X_j$ through any $X_k$ with $k\ge i,j$; a common upper bound proves independence of $k$ and naturality. Thus the universal property proves the assertion about this tail, rather than requiring a cofinality assertion without a size check.

source.place: A.1.5.11, first paragraph of proof, printed p. 806; explicit tail argument.

proof.text: We will repeatedly use the following colimit calculations. Compute a colimit under a root $R$ by adjoining a root vertex with value $R$ and its structure maps to the indexing diagram in $\mathcal A$. A cocone on the augmented diagram is precisely a cocone under $R$, including for the empty diagram. Base change sends $R\to V$ to $R'\to V\amalg_R R'$ and preserves such colimits and all specified pushout squares: maps out are pairs of maps agreeing on $R$. This same description gives $(V\amalg_R R')\amalg_{R'}R''\cong V\amalg_R R''$, compatible with all legs. For a nonempty filtered index, a cocone on a constant diagram is a single map, since any two indices have a common upper bound. Finally, iterated colimits commute whenever they exist: both sides represent families of maps compatible in both indices. We use these cocone descriptions below also when the support varies.

source.place: A.1.5.3 and universal-property calculations in A.1.5.11, printed pp. 800, 806-807; agent expansion.

proof.text: Call a descent a tuple $(i,S,V)$, where $i\in I$, $S\subseteq T$ is downward-closed with $|S|<\tau$, and $V$ is an $L$-tree on $S$ rooted at $X_i$, using exactly the specified $P_t\to Q_t$, equipped with a map of labelled trees to the original restriction on $S$. Require that its base change to $X$ is that original restriction, respecting every cell square. Every object of $V$, every predecessor colimit, and its total colimit $V_S$ is $\tau$-presentable. To check this, induct on the well-founded order: a predecessor colimit is the augmented colimit from Step 2; it has fewer than $\tau$ morphisms and presentable values. Apply [lem-coef-ordinary-small-colimit-presentable], then apply it to the finite span defining the cell pushout. Apply it once more to the augmented total diagram. The bound follows because an infinite set of cardinality less than $\tau$ has its square of that same cardinality; finite sets cause no problem. The root and both endpoints of every cell are presentable by hypothesis and the definition of a good tree. The empty-support descent at any $i$ has total object $X_i$.

source.place: A.1.5.1 and A.1.5.11, printed pp. 799-800, 806-807; presentability of all descended objects made explicit.

proof.text: Form a category $D$ of these descents. A morphism $(i,S,V)\to(j,S',V')$ requires $i\le j$, $S\subseteq S'$, has root map $X_i\to X_j$ from the fixed presentation, and is a map of the trees on $S$ to the restriction of $V'$ on $S$, fixing $P_t,Q_t$ and commuting with the maps to the original tree. Such a morphism, if it exists, is unique. On predecessors uniqueness follows from the colimit property; at a cell it follows from the pushout property and the fixed map on $Q_t$. Well-founded induction proves uniqueness throughout $S$. Composites have exactly the same restrictions and fixed cell maps, so $D$ is a preorder. It can be made small: [lem-coef-presentable-canonical-density] gives a small set of representatives of presentable objects. Represent each nonroot vertex of a descent by one of them, leaving its root $X_i$ fixed. There is a small set of choices of $i,S$, vertices, structure maps and comparison maps to the fixed $Y_t$, because $I,T$ and all Hom sets are small. The requirements on pushouts and comparisons are properties of these data. Every descent is isomorphic to one of these representatives; henceforth $D$ denotes this small preorder.

source.place: A.1.5.11, labelled descent data (a)-(c), printed pp. 806-807; agent category and smallness construction.

proof.text: Here is the construction of common upper descents, including prescribed support and root index. Given fewer than $\tau$ descents $d_a=(i_a,S_a,V^a)$, a set $E\subseteq T$ of size less than $\tau$, and an index $i_*\in I$, let $S$ be the downward closure of $E\cup\bigcup_a S_a$. It has size less than $\tau$: each individual element has fewer than $\tau$ predecessors and $\tau$ is regular. Choose $j_0\in I$ above $i_*$ and all $i_a$. Well-order the set $S$, then enumerate it by repeatedly selecting the first minimal remaining element. Until $S$ is exhausted, well-foundedness supplies a minimal remaining element, and the chosen well-order makes its choice definite. The selected elements are distinct, so the process stops before the successor cardinal of $|S|$; its stopping ordinal $\mu$ has cardinality $|S|<\tau$, hence $\mu<\tau$. If $S$ is empty take $\mu=0$. Every predecessor of a selected element lies in $S$ and was selected earlier, so all initial subsets $S_\alpha$ are downward-closed in $T$. We construct increasing $j_\alpha\in I$ and trees $W^\alpha$ on $S_\alpha$ over $X_{j_\alpha}$. The invariants are: base change to $X$ is the original tree on $S_\alpha$; all earlier constructed trees base change to the corresponding restrictions; and there are compatible morphisms from the restrictions of every $V^a$ on $S_a\cap S_\alpha$, fixing their cells. At zero take the empty tree over $X_{j_0}$. The following two steps give the successor and limit operations, so [lem-weil-pbc-transfinite-recursion] supplies the construction.

source.place: A.1.5.11, subsets (i)-(iv) and construction (a)-(c), printed pp. 806-807; agent extension with prescribed descents.

proof.text: At a successor let $t$ be the next cell, $B=\{s:s<t\}$, $j=j_\alpha$, and $A=W^\alpha_B$. Step 2 and the invariant identify $Y_B$ with $A\amalg_{X_j}X$ and with the colimit of $A\amalg_{X_j}X_k$ over $k\ge j$. This is a small $\tau$-filtered colimit by Step 1. Presentability of $P_t$ and clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] factor its original attaching map as $b:P_t\to A\amalg_{X_j}X_k\to Y_B$. For each $a$ with $t\in S_a$, downward closure gives $B\subseteq S_a$. The existing predecessor comparison gives another map $c_a:P_t\to V^a_B\to A$, whose image in $Y_B$ equals the original attaching map. Push $c_a$ to stage $k$. In the Hom-set colimit these maps and $b$ agree. Clause (3) of the cited elementwise lemma supplies a stage where each equality holds. There are fewer than $\tau$ such requirements; choose a single upper bound $l$ of all their witness indices in $I$. Base-change the processed tree to $X_l$ and attach the cell $P_t\to Q_t$ using the image of $b$. The equalities just enforced induce maps from each $V^a_t$ to this new cell by its defining pushout, with the identity on $Q_t$ and $P_t$. For $t\notin S_a$ no new component is required. The new attaching map becomes the specified original one after pushing out to $X$, so uniqueness of pushouts extends that comparison. All order-map and composition conditions follow by equality on predecessor cocone legs and the $Q_t$ leg. This proves the full successor invariant, not just existence of an unlabeled pushout.

source.place: A.1.5.11, successor displayed tail colimit and factorization, printed p. 807; simultaneous equality uses Stacks 04AX, section-directed-colimits, and its existing node.

proof.text: At a nonzero limit $\lambda\le\mu$, take an upper bound $j_\lambda$ of $\{j_\alpha:\alpha<\lambda\}$. There are fewer than $\tau$ indices. Base-change the earlier processed trees to $X_{j_\lambda}$. For a cell choose any earlier stage containing it; the transition invariant identifies the choices by the unique isomorphisms fixing the root and all cell legs. Every order arrow occurs in an earlier stage containing its target, and each entire predecessor set occurs as soon as that target does. Consequently these diagrams and their pushout squares glue to a tree on $S_\lambda=\bigcup_{\alpha<\lambda}S_\alpha$. The maps from the $V^a$ glue as well, since their restrictions are unique by Step 4. This preserves all invariants. At $\mu$ we obtain a descent on $S$ over $X_{j_\mu}$, with morphisms from all $d_a$ and with $j_\mu\ge i_*$. Its objects and total object are presentable by Step 3. This proves the upper-bound assertion of Step 5, including the case of no given descents and $S=\varnothing$.

source.place: A.1.5.11, limit stage, printed p. 807; agent expansion of compatibility and prescribed-descent invariant.

proof.text: By Steps 5-7, every subset of $D$ of size less than $\tau$, including the empty one, has an upper bound. Thus this small preorder is $\tau$-filtered. Quotient its objects by $d\sim d'$ if $d\le d'\le d$, to obtain a small $\tau$-filtered poset $P$, and select one representative for each class. Equivalent descents have the same root index and support, since $I$ and the inclusion order on subsets are antisymmetric. Their unique inverse maps are isomorphisms fixing every label. Therefore representatives give a genuine diagram of descents on $P$: for $p\le p'$ use the unique morphism in $D$. Compositions and identities agree by uniqueness. Put $M_p=X_{i(p)}$, $N_p=V^p_{S_p}$, and $h_p:M_p\to N_p$. The total maps are induced by the common-cell maps and the inclusions of the supports. Step 3 gives presentable endpoints. Root comparisons, pushout identifications, and compatibility with both legs of every cell are precisely the data defining $D$. Taking no prescribed descents in Step 5 shows that every $E$ of size less than $\tau$ is contained in some $S_p$.

source.place: A.1.5.11, compatible descent data; agent preorder-to-poset construction for A.2.6.9 observation (ii).

proof.text: The root diagram $p\mapsto M_p$ has colimit $X$. For each $i\in I$ there is an empty-support descent $e_i$, and $i\le j$ gives $e_i\le e_j$. Any descent $d$ at root $X_i$ receives a morphism $e_i\to d$ acting as the identity on that root. Hence a cocone on the roots of the $P$-diagram is exactly a cocone on $(X_i)_{i\in I}$: restrict to the classes $[e_i]$; in the other direction assign to a descent at $i$ the leg at $i$. The empty-support morphisms force the two operations to be inverse, even when a different representative of $[e_i]$ was selected, since its root is still $X_i$. Step 1 and the colimit universal property now identify the root colimit with $X$.

source.place: Agent cocone argument for the compact-root presentation in A.2.6.9 observation (ii).

proof.text: Let now $Q\subseteq P$ be any nonempty filtered subposet, with no $\tau$-filteredness assumption. Set $S=\bigcup_{q\in Q}S_q$ and $M=\operatorname{colim}_{q\in Q}M_q$. For $t\in S$ let $J_t=\{q\in Q:t\in S_q\}$. It is nonempty and filtered, and every $q\in Q$ has an upper bound in $J_t$, by taking a common upper bound with an index containing $t$. Restriction to $J_t$ does not change a colimit: extend a tail cocone using such an upper bound, with independence checked at a second common upper bound as in Step 1. Define $Z_t=\operatorname{colim}_{q\in J_t}V^q_t$. These carry maps from $M$ because $\operatorname{colim}_{J_t}M_q=M$. For $s<t$ one has $J_t\subseteq J_s$, so the component order maps induce $Z_s\to Z_t$; their composition laws follow on the colimit legs. The predecessor object $Z_{<t}$ in $M/\mathcal A$ equals $\operatorname{colim}_{q\in J_t}V^q_{<t}$. Indeed every $q\in J_t$ contains all of $B=\{s:s<t\}$. Applying the augmented-cocone description of Step 2, cocones on either object are exactly a map from $M$ and compatible maps on the $s$-vertices for $s\in B$, with their root and order relations. One may compute every $Z_s$ here over $J_t$, which is cofinal in $J_s$ by the same common-upper-bound argument. This proves the predecessor comparison including $B=\varnothing$.

source.place: Agent filtered-union construction expanding the compatible descent use in A.2.6.9 (ii); only cocone universal properties.

proof.text: For $t\in S$, the maps on fixed cell labels are identities, so the colimits of the constant $P_t$ and $Q_t$ diagrams on $J_t$ are $P_t$ and $Q_t$. Take the colimit of the specified cell squares there. Maps from its proposed apex to $H$ are compatible pairs of maps from $V^q_{<t}$ and $Q_t$ agreeing on $P_t$; filteredness makes the $Q_t$-map independent of the index. Step 10 therefore identifies the result with the pushout square $P_t\to Q_t$, $Z_{<t}\to Z_t$. This proves that $Z$ is an $L$-tree on $S$, with exactly the specified cells and root $M$. Its total colimit is $\operatorname{colim}_{q\in Q}N_q$: a compatible cocone on the latter is a compatible family on every descended tree, including roots. Such families are precisely cocones on the augmented union diagram with vertices $M,Z_t$. Every cell occurs somewhere and every finite collection of root, cell or order relations occurs at a common upper index in $Q$. This gives inverse assignments of cocones and proves the claimed identification. It also identifies its root arrow with the arrow-category colimit $h_Q$: a commuting square out of that arrow is exactly compatible squares out of the $h_q$.

source.place: Agent cocone proof of cellularity for arbitrary filtered subposets; fixed-label compatibility is essential here.

proof.text: Keep $Q,S,M,Z_t,N_Q$ from Steps 10-11. Apply [lem-coef-ordinary-directed-cover-colimit] to the augmented ordinary poset $S^\lhd$ (one new root vertex preceding every cell), covered by its full subposets $S_q^\lhd$, and to the original diagram with root $X$. The index $Q$ is small, nonempty and filtered. Its supports increase, cover $S$, and contain the root at every stage, including when $S$ is empty. The ambient category has all small colimits by hypothesis. By Step 2 the restricted colimit cocones have apices $Y_{S_q}$, and the total cocone has apex $Y_S$. The lemma identifies $\operatorname{colim}_{q\in Q}Y_{S_q}$ with $Y_S$, respecting precisely the transition maps and every restricted cocone leg. No comparison with enhanced categories is needed.

source.place: Agent-formulated directed-cover assembly lemma from Categories Definition 002F (definition-colimit, lines 1310-1329). Tag 002F supplies the universal property, not a separately numbered directed-cover assertion; directedness is explicitly defined in the statement. The argument extracted from former Step 12 of lem-coef-cellular-tree-presentable-approximations is recorded in report.md.

proof.text: At each $q$, the descent data and Step 2 give the specified pushout square with top $M_q\to N_q$ and bottom $X\to Y_{S_q}$. The squares form a $Q$-diagram because the descent maps respect the comparisons. Apply [lem-coef-colimits-of-pushout-squares]. The lower left corner is the colimit of the constant $X$ diagram, canonically $X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-constant-connected-diagram], since $Q$ is nonempty filtered and hence connected. Step 12 identifies the lower right corner with $Y_S$. The resulting square has top $h_Q:M\to N_Q$ and the required canonical legs, and is a pushout. Thus $N_Q\amalg_M X\cong Y_S$ by the displayed comparison, rather than by an unspecified isomorphism.

source.place: A.1.5.6 and A.1.5.3, printed pp. 800-801; agent filtered-union and pushout calculation supplying A.2.6.9 observation (ii). Repair: extract colimit comparisons into cited general statements.

proof.text: For the objectwise comparison fix $t\in S$ and use the nonempty filtered tail $J_t$ from Step 10. At each of its indices the specified square has corners $M_q,V^q_t,X,Y_t$ and is a pushout. Apply [lem-coef-colimits-of-pushout-squares] over $J_t$. Step 10 gives the upper corners $M,Z_t$, and [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-constant-connected-diagram] gives the lower corners $X,Y_t$, with their specified legs. Hence the comparison $Z_t\amalg_M X\to Y_t$ is an isomorphism. These comparisons respect every order arrow, attaching map and $Q_t$ leg: after precomposing with each stage cocone leg both composites are the specified original maps, and uniqueness in the colimit property makes them equal. For predecessor objects take the diagram on the augmented predecessor poset $\{s:s<t\}^\lhd$, including its root. The squares just obtained, with the identity root square, form a diagram of pushouts. This index is nonempty connected because it has an initial root. The same two cited lemmas identify its colimit square with the square on $M,Z_{<t},X,Y_{<t}$, by Step 2. It is therefore a pushout even when $t$ has no predecessors.

source.place: A.1.5.6 and A.1.5.3, printed pp. 800-801; agent filtered-union and pushout calculation supplying A.2.6.9 observation (ii). Repair: extract colimit comparisons into cited general statements.

proof.text: Steps 10-11 already give an actual $L$-tree on $S$ whose root arrow is $h_Q$. Apply the weak-saturation conclusion of [lem-coef-weak-saturation-tree-presentation] with $\varnothing\subseteq S$. It puts $h_Q$ in the weakly saturated closure of $L$; no closure under arbitrary filtered colimits is used. Now take $Q=P$. Step 8 gives $S=T$ and Step 9 identifies $M_P\to X$ as an isomorphism induced by the root cocone. The pushout square of Step 13 then identifies $N_P\to Y_T$ as an isomorphism. With Step 11's arrow-colimit calculation, this proves that the specified cocone to $X\to Y_T$ is colimiting. For $T=\varnothing$, all supports are empty and all root arrows are identities, so the same argument applies.
